Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

address verb

speak to; call by a name or title

also address someone, speak to someone, form of address, address a crowd

classical

Liv. 22.30.2: cum patrem Fabium appellāsset
Cic. Q. fr. 2.8.1: ut mē et appellēs et interpellēs

appellō, appellāre, appellāvī, appellātum

verb, first conjugation

address, speak to; call (someone by a name or title)

Lewis & Short: “to accost, address, to speak to, call upon (very freq. and class.)”; with two accusatives, to address someone as something. Not appellō, appellere, drive towards.

Other words

  • alloquor, alloquī, allocūtus sum — speak to, address (a person or a crowd)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Ter. And. 343b: Cessās adloquī?; Traupman 176, 268: senātum adloquentur, will address the senate

    Also spelled adloquor. Lewis & Short: rare before Augustus (twice in Cicero), common after; used of a general addressing his troops. A speech to a gathering is ōrātiō (see speech).

Examples

  • cum patrem Fabium appellāsset

    when he had addressed Fabius as “father”Liv. 22.30.2

  • tū vērō ut mē et appellēs et interpellēs et obloquāre et colloquāre velim. quid enim mihi suāvius?

    I do want you to speak to me, interrupt me, contradict me, talk with me. What could be sweeter to me?Cic. Q. fr. 2.8.1

  • Cessās adloquī?

    What are you waiting for? Speak to him!Ter. And. 343b

See also speech, name, address.
